result.text:
801: \end{equation}
802: with $c_{-,1}=c_{+,1}=1$ for an empty history.  It satisfies
803: \eqref{eq:relative-endpoint-sandwich} and
804: $\ell^2\le c_{-,t}\le1\le c_{+,t}\le\ell^{-2}$.
805: Either certificate can be used in \Cref{cor:relative-endpoint-ucb}.
806: \end{corollary}
807: 
808: These certificates compare scalar weights on fixed feature directions;
809: they make no claim about general gradient rotation.  Maintaining the counts
810: and one collection-weight sum per category makes
811: \eqref{eq:tanh-category-relative} computable from current category projections
812: without an eigensolve or a scan of the full history.  This reduces the work
813: needed for an endpoint certificate, not the cost of all width or center
814: solves, and does not itself imply improved regret.  The appendix gives the
815: termwise proof and a case where the endpoint distance is zero although the
816: synthetic path has positive length.
817: 
818: The previous additive stacked-design result remains a useful local corollary.
819: If $\chi_t<1$ and
820: \begin{equation}\label{eq:local-additive-new}
821:  (1-\chi_t)^2\bVbar_t\preceq\bV_t
822:  \preceq(1+\chi_t)^2\bVbar_t,
823: \end{equation}
824: use the local score obtained from \eqref{eq:transported-score-new} by replacing
825: $e^{\bar D_t/2}$ with $1+\chi_t$.
826: \begin{corollary}[Local small-drift transport]
827: \label{cor:local-small-drift-new}
828: Under the remaining hypotheses of \Cref{thm:transported-ucb}, the local score
829: satisfies
830: \begin{align}
831: R_T
832: &\le\sqrt{\left(\sigma^2+\frac{G^2}{\lambda}\right)\gamma_T
833: \sum_{t=1}^T\beta_t^2
834: \left[1+\alpha_t\frac{1+\chi_t}{1-\chi_t}
835: \sqrt{\frac{\kappa_{+,t}}{\kappa_{-,t}}}\right]^2}
836: \nonumber\\
837: &\quad+2\sum_{t=1}^Tb_t(a_t)+\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t.
838: \label{eq:local-small-drift-regret-new}
839: \end{align}
840: \end{corollary}
841: Neither the local factor nor the exponential factor uniformly dominates the
842: other because they summarize different paths.

871: \paragraph{Scope.}
872: The abstract theorem applies to any estimator that supplies
873: \eqref{eq:abstract-confidence-new}.  A complete exponential-family
874: specialization would additionally require a likelihood-score confidence event,
875: prediction conversion, pre-reward collection-time Fisher weights, control of
876: weight and Jacobian transport, and an information-potential bound.  The factor
877: geometry above does not establish those statistical steps, so no such theorem
878: is claimed here.
